recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Handle FHIR-54324 or any terminology migration separately when final Applied/Published source work is in scope; do not reinterpret FHIR-5824 as requiring Device.status itself to carry physical availability after later OO decisions split the concepts.
issue_request: FHIR-5824 asked OO to add a Device.status element because Device had no way to indicate that a device was no longer available, including lost, expired, destroyed, contaminated, or entered-in-error cases.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-5824 was found in current git history. The issue is marked Applied for DSTU1, and Device.status is present in current source; current git history imports it during the 2021 build-source/R4B work. Later commit 0cd35c3c18 explicitly applied FHIR-32557 and FHIR-34542 by changing Device.status from availability semantics to Device record status and adding Device.availabilityStatus.
additional_context: FHIR-32557 is the main later decision: Device.status is about the Device record, while Device.availabilityStatus is about physical device availability. FHIR-46962 later corrected the Device notes to identify availabilityStatus, and FHIR-53243 re-added unknown to the Device record status code system. FHIR-54324 is a later Resolved - change required issue proposing additional availabilityStatus terminology changes, but it is not yet Applied/Published and does not make FHIR-5824 incomplete.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Device is active in source/fhir.ini, Device.status exists with a required binding to ValueSet/device-status, Device.availabilityStatus exists with an extensible binding to ValueSet/device-availability-status, and the Device notes distinguish record status from device availability.
